title: Ordinary exchange preserves the canonical constant-object unit
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $v:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$, $w:Y'\to Y$ be a commutative square, so $v;f=f';w$. Write $C_T=A_T[0]$ for the ordinary derived constant object and $Lh^*,Rh_*$ for the functors of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Write $c_h:Lh^*C_{\mathrm{target}(h)}\cong C_{\mathrm{source}(h)}$ for its canonical constant-object pullback comparison, and $\eta_h:C_{\mathrm{target}(h)}\to Rh_*C_{\mathrm{source}(h)}$ for supportedDerivedUnit of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-system]. Let $\mathrm{Ex}:Lw^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lv^*$ be the derived exchange mate of the square [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Then $Lw^*(\eta_f);\mathrm{Ex}_{C_X};Rf'_*(c_v.\mathrm{hom})=c_w.\mathrm{hom};\eta_{f'}$. No Cartesian, properness, finite-ring or nonempty-scheme hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Reuse the existing proved ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback_comp to identify the constant-object comparison on either composite of the square. Cancel the derived composition isomorphism, obtaining the constant-object pullback comparison square. A proved private cache aligns the stored derived-category instances without repeating the source-library single-object calculation.

Expand supportedDerivedUnit as the derived adjunction unit followed by direct image of the constant-object pullback comparison. Use naturality to move the comparison past exchange. Apply unit_mateEquiv, substitute the first-step comparison square, and use naturality of the second adjunction unit.

theorem ordinaryFiniteConstant_baseChange (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {v : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {w : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (sq : CommSq v f' f w) :
    (ordinaryFinitePullback A w).map (supportedDerivedUnit A f) ≫
        (derivedBaseChangeMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq).app (ordinaryFiniteUnit A X) ≫
        (ordinaryFinitePushforward A f').map (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A v).hom =
      (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A w).hom ≫ supportedDerivedUnit A f'
